title: 1983 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Point \(D\) is on side \(CB\) of triangle \(ABC.\) If \(\angle CAD=\angle DAB=60^\circ,\) \(AC=3\) and \(AB=6,\) then the length of \(AD\) is

solutions.text:
By the angle bisector theorem, write \(CD=t\) and \(DB=2t.\) Let \(AD=d.\) The law of cosines in triangles \(ACD\) and \(ABD,\) whose angles at \(A\) are both \(60^\circ,\) gives \[ \begin{aligned} t^2&=9+d^2-3d,\\ 4t^2&=36+d^2-6d. \end{aligned} \] Subtracting four times the first equation from the second yields \(0=-3d^2+6d.\) Since \(d\gt0,\) \(d=2.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
